title: Bathroom Size Code-Clearance Dataset
description:
Every full bathroom and half bathroom size, inch by inch, checked against the International Residential Code (IRC) clearance minimums (R307.1, P2708.1): which standard layouts fit, which do not, and the exact check each failing layout breaks. 26,628 room-size × door combinations (8,876 room sizes × in-swing, out-swing and pocket doors) and 106,512 layout checks across 84 distinct layouts.

Two findings: a full bath fits at least one standard layout if and only if the short wall is at least 5 ft and the long wall at least 6 ft 6 in (smallest: 32.5 sq ft); and for half baths the door decides it — re-hanging an in-swing door to swing out rescues 55% of failing sizes and shrinks the smallest workable half bath from 17.8 to 15.3 sq ft, while a pocket door rescues far fewer.

Every row is produced by the layout engine of FitsTheRoom, which draws these same layouts to scale for any room, so the data matches the plans on the site exactly. "Fails" means none of the four standard layouts fits, not that no bathroom is possible; local codes may be stricter than the IRC. Released under CC0 1.0.
